physics_urdf.description: Optional collision-only URDF generated for this execution under .artimo-runs/<task_id>/. The source task URDF remains authoritative for the mechanism.

base_support_height_m.description: Height of the physical plinth under the robot. Its collision footprint is derived from the grounded robot base link AABB, and it participates in placement, swept-clearance, rollout contact, and rendering.

contact_sequence.description: Adjacent robot-contact stages with the same value form one uninterrupted grasp. The harness approaches once, preserves contact between stages, and retreats only after the final stage.

release_before_phase.description: Optional explicit release boundary. The harness retains the grasp through this stage and any intervening plan phases, then opens the fingers and removes a disclosed ideal attachment immediately before the named later plan phase.

interaction.description: Invariant benchmark policy: physical_push for maintain_width controls; disclosed explicit_ideal_feasibility for open_then_close grasps. Frictional force-closure tuning is outside this benchmark.

precontact_offset_m.description: Non-negative distance from the grasp target farther into free space along contact-pose local +Z. Robot approach moves in local -Z.

grasp_depth_m.description: Final manipulation standoff of the Panda grasptarget from the contacted surface along outward contact local +Z. This remains after approach and is not approach clearance; validate it from measured per-finger target gaps. precontact_offset_m is the separate transient free-space distance. The generic harness maps contact-frame +Z to Panda-grasptarget -Z.

robot_tool_contact_offset_eef_m.description: Optional vector in the robot end-effector link frame from the EEF origin to the actual robot tool surface that must coincide with contact_pose_link. Use for maintain_width physical pushes such as one selected fingertip; the harness subtracts the rotated vector when solving the EEF origin. Omit for centered parallel-jaw grasps.

mode.description: Agent-selected contact acquisition. Use open_then_close for a grasp that must surround the target before closing; use maintain_width when a pre-shaped or closed gripper is itself the pushing/pressing tool.

approach_finger_opening_m.description: Finger joint position during transit and approach. For open_then_close it must exceed finger_opening_m; for maintain_width it must equal finger_opening_m.

close_s.description: Time used to interpolate from approach_finger_opening_m to finger_opening_m while the arm holds the first contact pose. Must be positive for open_then_close and zero for maintain_width.

settle_s.description: Time to hold the acquired contact before object manipulation begins.

release_s.description: Time used to reopen at the final contact pose before retreat. Must be positive for open_then_close and zero for maintain_width.

manipulation_sample_hold_s.description: Physical dwell for each of the 65 ordered object-path samples. Increase it to execute the same plan path more slowly without changing any object endpoint or replaying object motion.

approach_waypoints_link_m.description: Ordered via-points for the transit into the precontact pose, expressed in the contacted link frame. Use these to route the wrist around an intervening link instead of straight through it.

transit_waypoints_world.description: Ordered world-frame end-effector poses used only while transiting from the preceding released retreat endpoint (or home for the first stage) to this stage's approach. Use geometry-derived poses to route around obstacles moved by earlier plan stages; these poses are not replayed during this stage's retreat.

release_retreat_waypoints_world.description: Agent-planned end-effector poses executed after opening the fingers and before release_before_phase begins. They must place the whole robot outside the released mechanism's swept volume.

minimum_release_swept_clearance_m.description: Required whole-robot separation from every object link while moving through release_retreat_waypoints_world and while the declared passive-return joints sweep to rest.

forbidden_contact_links.description: Object links the robot must stay clear of while approaching this stage. Checked at planning time against the whole swept path, so a candidate that would strike them is rejected before any rollout.

minimum_swept_clearance_m.description: Required separation from forbidden_contact_links along the approach and manipulation path.

control_execution.description: Exhaustive, auditable ownership of every plan timeline control. Ownership is per control rather than per phase because one phase may combine a passive return with a different internally actuated motion.

energy_source.description: Physical source that performs an internal-mechanism control after the robot trigger. Desired motion or a phase name is not an energy source.

justification.description: Required human-auditable reason for any internal mechanism; it must describe the trigger/transmission rather than merely restate the desired motion.

release.description: Second, later object-side phase reached when the measured driver returns toward rest. Models a plan phase such as a lid closing after a pedal is released; without it a latched effect could never return.

settle_s.description: Seconds the robot holds at home after the last stage. Must be long enough for any declared causal release to reach its plan endpoint.

ik.description: Bounded initial-contact IK search budget. Dense manipulation always follows the nearest local joint-space branch; pose tolerances and joint-step rejection are not task parameters.
